stage: 6b. Run day to day: disputes and fraud

summary.text: Every network runs the same skeleton: a fraud report or claim, a chargeback, a response, pre-arbitration, then a ruling. Each wraps it in its own tool, vocabulary and clock.
Mastercard is the most visible. Its public Mastercom spec names 13 work queues, case statuses from New to Ruled, and hard edits that reject late cycles.
Visa keeps VROL screens and API states restricted. What partners see is inferred from processor portals that mirror VROL statuses, questionnaires and buttons.
American Express publishes the clearest merchant dispute screen. Its summary table sorts cases into Response Needed, Review in Progress and Closed, and each case shows days left to respond.
The contest has moved before the chargeback. Visa switched Rapid Dispute Resolution on for issuers by default, and Mastercard pulls Ethoca data into the claim itself.
Monitoring now counts fraud and disputes together at portfolio level, and merchants and payfacs cannot see the items behind their own ratio.
Small issuers, fintechs and most merchants never touch a network dispute tool. Processors translate network stages into their own states, windows and codes.
The Discover family is the least visible. Its Disputes Portal is fully gated, its public merchant help page lists Internet Explorer 6, and PULSE dispute rules need a login.
The strongest openings for Discover are one shared case vocabulary, a published monitoring line, free pre-dispute resolution, and fraud reporting folded into the dispute.

how_it_works.text: The issuer must report fraud to Visa before it can raise a fraud dispute, within 60 days of the transaction.
An analyst logs into VROL, searches the transaction, records provisional credit, opens a dispute case and completes a dynamic questionnaire.
Fraud and authorisation disputes follow the Allocation flow, where Visa assigns liability and the acquirer can only pre-arbitrate within 30 days.
Consumer and processing disputes follow the Collaboration flow, where the issuer makes the pre-arbitration attempt within 30 days of the acquirer's response.
Arbitration must be filed within 10 days of the pre-arbitration response, and a missed deadline closes the cycle against the silent party.
Time limits vary by condition. Authorisation disputes allow 75 days against 120 for most fraud and consumer disputes.
Before a dispute exists, VROL checks Order Insight and Rapid Dispute Resolution. RDR-resolved cases close with status Merchant Credit.
Issuers with excessive card-absent disputes or fraud enter VIMP, with assessments rising to USD 100,000 a month.
Compromised-account alerts arrive only inside Visa Risk Manager, and loss recovery needs fraud reported within 120 days of the alert.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Resolve Online (VROL)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Mandated web tool on Visa Online for the whole dispute cycle. Questions and documents must be in English.

tools_and_screens.name: VROL dispute questionnaire
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Sections for transaction, dispute request, elaboration, certifications, notes and documents, and issuer contact, as mirrored by a processor portal.

tools_and_screens.name: VROL Dispute Tracking Scorecard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Case tracking view used with Visa's outsourced dispute service.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Risk Manager
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Rules, case, account and reporting modules over the Advanced Authorization score, plus an Alert API into the issuer back office.

tools_and_screens.name: Dispute Doc Analyzer (2026)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Summaries of merchant documents for issuer analysts, pitched against slow manual review.

friction.text: Compelling Evidence 3.0 reaches the issuer as a Visa rejection code with no dispute right left, and ICBA says it shifts liability and call-centre work to issuers.
Arbitration is decided on prior exchanges only, and an appeal needs new evidence and at least USD 5,000 at stake.
Fraud-reporting failures can suspend fraud dispute rights for 90 or 180 days, turning an administrative lapse into direct losses.
Every US issuer pays Advanced Authorization fees whether or not it uses the data.

how_it_works.text: The issuer opens one claim in Mastercom, and every later event hangs off that claim ID.
A fraud chargeback needs a prior Fraud and Loss Database report, which the issuer can file from inside the claim.
Evidence must reach Mastercom within eight days, second presentment comes within 45, and pre-arbitration within 30 after that.
If the acquirer rejects pre-arbitration, the issuer has 15 days to escalate to arbitration or it bears the loss.
Mastercom stamps some chargebacks as rejected before the acquirer sees them, including 5002 for First-Party Trust.
Ethoca Consumer Clarity data is being linked into the claim record for issuer agents during 2026.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercom work queues
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: IssuerRepresentmentUnworked, IssuerWorked, Rejects, PendingDocumentation, SenderCaseFiling, ReceiverCaseFiling and Closed, among 13 queues.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercom case filing
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Case types 1 to 4, a mandatory memo up to 13,000 characters, statuses New to Ruled, and six ruling values such as Favor Sender.

tools_and_screens.name: First-Party Trust evidence flag
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The issuer must acknowledge merchant evidence before proceeding with a chargeback.

tools_and_screens.name: Fraud and Loss Database
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Batch, screen or API submission. Records land as confirmed, rejected or suspended.

friction.text: Overriding a First-Party Trust reject needs a notarised cardholder affidavit plus a closed and blocked account.
Fraud chargebacks are capped at 35 per card account by the Fraud Notification Service.
A claim opened in Mastercom v6 cannot be recreated in Mastercom Extended, so issuers track where each claim lives during migration.
Mastercard, which sells dispute tools, says US issuers spend about USD 9 to 10 per dispute.

how_it_works.text: Amex first tries to resolve the disputed charge from its own information, then sends an Inquiry or a Chargeback.
On the GNS network, issuers file a First Chargeback within 120 days, and acquirers have 45 days to second present.
GNS issuers must report confirmed fraud by the next business day after verification.
The Global Disputes Monitoring Program holds each issuer and acquirer to monthly regional thresholds, 0.20 per cent in the US.

tools_and_screens.name: AEGNS Network Disputes Manager (NDM)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The licensed dispute system for all GNS documentation, with a USD 100 monthly licence and a free browser version, NDM Disputes Online.

tools_and_screens.name: GNS FraudNet
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Urgent Investigation Requests, the Participant Communication Platform and monthly fraud reports, reached after Knowledge Base access.

friction.text: Arbitration costs USD 150 to file and USD 250 for review, and a USD 100 penalty may be assessed when submission rules are not followed.
The NDM and FraudNet user guides are on the gated Knowledge Base, so no screens are public.

how_it_works.text: Discover's dispute framework charges a dispute resolved for the cardholder back to the merchant or acquirer.
Issuer-side dispute screens and filing windows are not public. The Disputes Portal redirects straight to a sign-in.
Confirmed fraud is submitted through a separate Confirmed Fraud Portal enrolled by form.
Compromise cases run through Account Incident Manager, shared between issuers, acquirers and the network.
Diners Club franchises enrol in the same Account Incident Manager through a dedicated form section and mailbox.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover Network Disputes Portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated behind the same identity provider as the Partner Product Portal. Nothing readable without credentials.

tools_and_screens.name: Fraud and Risk Center
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Login hub for Account Incident Manager, Confirmed Fraud, Fraud Alerts and High Brand Risk, with email-only MFA since 2025.

friction.text: Fraud tool enrolment needs two named administrators, a Director or VP signature and an emailed form.

best_pattern.text: Mastercard's claim model is the best issuer pattern: one claim ID from intake to ruling, fraud reporting inside the claim, and named queues with hard deadline edits.

discover_today.text: Discover's issuer dispute experience is not publicly visible. Fraud reporting and compromise cases sit in separate portals enrolled by signed forms.

by_partner.partner_type: Issuers: community banks and credit unions

how_it_works.text: Front-line staff judge chargeback rights across Visa, CO-OP, PULSE and MAP rules before a back-office specialist files.
Card staff review a daily Visa exception file and work disputes in VROL.
A credit union collects every questionnaire answer before filing, because VROL rejects incomplete disputes.
Compromise alerts often arrive through the processor, and staff reformat the list as a CSV and upload it by hand.
Regulation E runs its own clock: a decision in 10 business days, or provisional credit then up to 45 days.

tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Worldpay's Disputes API sold to payfacs and ISOs uses stage codes such as CH1 and PAB, and flags Visa RDR cases.

The FTC's 2026 orders against Nuvei and Humboldt centre on chargeback screening failures.

design_moves.title: Show whose move it is and the days left, on every case
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: Make the case status a next action with an owner and a day count, drawn from the condition's own time limit. Publish the same states through the API.
design_moves.why_advantage: Amex and a PULSE processor wrapper already show next action and days left. Each fintech processor invents its own states, so one network vocabulary would travel across all of them.

design_moves.title: Put the partner's own legal clock beside the network clock
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Show Reg E provisional credit and decision deadlines next to chargeback deadlines on each issuer case, starting from the cardholder contact date.
design_moves.why_advantage: Issuers run two sets of deadlines. The only public tool that warns on the Reg E deadline is a processor portal, so a network that does it serves small issuers directly.

design_moves.title: Let the cardholder start the claim and let the network set the clock
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Offer issuers a network-hosted claim start they can embed in their app, feeding the case with a network-set timer for each step.
design_moves.why_advantage: Pix mandates in-app self-service with central-bank timers. Card claims still start by phone or branch, and some fintechs see them a day late.

design_moves.title: Fold fraud reporting into the dispute
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Let one issuer action file the fraud report and open the dispute, instead of a separate Confirmed Fraud portal.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard both require the fraud report first, and Visa penalises reporting failures by suspending dispute rights. Mastercard already files the report from inside the claim.

design_moves.title: Offer free pre-dispute resolution and count it as prevented
partner_types: Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: Route every new claim through a merchant resolution step first, at no per-alert fee, and show resolved claims as prevented on partner reports.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa auto-enrolled issuers in RDR and excludes pre-dispute resolutions from monitoring. Merchants pay per alert elsewhere, and Mastercard's acquirer route is reported to be ending.

design_moves.title: Publish the monitoring line and show the items behind the ratio
partner_types: Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: Publish Discover's dispute and fraud thresholds. Give acquirers a live ratio per merchant and sub-merchant with every counted item listed.
design_moves.why_advantage: Merchants cannot see the items behind VAMP and data arrives a month late. Discover has no public line at all, so publishing one closes a gap competitors leave open.

design_moves.title: Let evidence be checked before it is final
partner_types: Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: Validate evidence against the reason code before submission, show limits up front, and list items still missing inside the window.
design_moves.why_advantage: CE3.0 and Stripe Issuing allow one attempt. Upload caps range from three images to 18 MB. Mastercom's Pending Documentation Report shows the value of flagging gaps early.

design_moves.title: Deliver compromise alerts as actions
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Send compromised-card alerts as a list with block, monitor and reissue actions per card, by screen and API, with the recovery deadline shown.
design_moves.why_advantage: Credit unions reformat alert lists by hand several times a week. Vendors now sell tools against that work, and loss recovery depends on reporting within 120 days.

design_moves.title: Make the dispute rules public and dated
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Publish the Discover and PULSE dispute rules and time limits openly, with effective dates on each change.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard publishes its Chargeback Guide and Visa its core rules. Discover and PULSE keep theirs gated, so practitioners fill the gap with secondhand figures.

design_moves.title: One sign-in and self-serve enrolment for dispute and fraud tools
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Put the Disputes Portal and the Fraud and Risk Center under one identity, with administrators granting access online.
design_moves.why_advantage: Discover's fraud tools need signed forms and email-only MFA, while the Disputes Portal already uses the shared identity provider.

design_moves.title: Give intermediaries a multi-institution queue and give the client a view
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Let a processor or CUSO work cases for many clients in one queue, while each client sees its own cases read-only.
design_moves.why_advantage: Small issuers and fintechs reach networks through processors and learn outcomes late or never. Amex OptBlue merchants see no network screen at all.

design_moves.title: Structured ATM claims built on the journal
design_moves.move: Ask for named journal fields in ATM claims and responses in place of free-text memos.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa names the disbursement record fields while Mastercard codes ATM cases as free text, and operators already hold the journal.
